chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād and al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man doubted in the maghrib prayer and did not know whether he had prayed two rakʿahs or three.
He said: “He gives salām, then stands and adds one rakʿah to it.”
Then he said: “This, by Allah, is among that which is never made up.”
And what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād al-Nāb, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who did not know whether he had prayed the fajr prayer as two rakʿahs or one rakʿah. He said: “He recites the tashahhud and leaves, then stands and prays one rakʿah. If he had prayed two rakʿahs, then this would be supererogatory; and if he had prayed one rakʿah, then this would complete the prayer.”

I said: And if he prayed maghrib and did not know whether he had prayed two or three? He said: “He recites the tashahhud and leaves, then stands and prays one rakʿah. If he had prayed three, then this would be supererogatory; and if he had prayed two, then this would complete the prayer. And this, by Allah, is among that which is never made up.”

key_terms.الْفَجْرَ: the fajr prayer, the two-rakʿah dawn salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib prayer, the three-rakʿah evening salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَمَامَ الصَّلَاةِ: the completion and fulfillment of the prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَةً: a single rakʿah, one unit of salat (prayer)
key_terms.شَكَّ: doubted or became uncertain during prayer
key_terms.لَا يُقْضَى: it is not made up later as qaḍāʾ
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدُ: he recites the tashahhud before ending the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts the number of rakʿahs in fajr or maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the ruling for one who doubts whether he has completed the required number of rakʿahs in fajr or maghrib prayer. He completes the prayer outwardly, then adds one rakʿah; if the original prayer was complete, the added rakʿah counts as supererogatory, and if it was incomplete, it completes the obligatory prayer.
